title: Unified Inference: Q2 Product Overview, PRD, Roadmap & Pricing (vNext)
author: Ava Chen
content:
Summary

This document describes the Q2 product scope for Unified Inference (vNext): the product overview, high-level PRD and requirements, detailed design specs for API and Console changes, roadmap and themes for the next three quarters, pricing and packaging notes, and release notes for the initial canary. The intent is to align engineering, product, sales, and customer success on delivery milestones, success metrics, and rollout strategy.

Context and background
- Unified Inference is Redwood's core product that provides a consistent runtime and API across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. This initiative focuses on improving pricing transparency, adding enterprise-grade rollout controls, and shipping performance-driven defaults for common workloads.
- The vNext release bundles: performance/throughput improvements, model routing/fallback policies, new pricing tiers and packaging for Reserved Capacity, and console UX improvements for rollout control and cost observability.

Goals (what success looks like)
1. Deliver an API and console experience that enables customers to: pin model versions, configure rollout policies (canary / A/B / gradual), and observe per-route cost/latency within the Redwood Console.
2. Ship pricing and packaging updates that reduce customer unit cost by at least 15% for common chat/text workloads through smarter defaults (batching, caching, quantization recommendations).
3. Increase conversion from trial to Dedicated (reserved capacity) by 20% for mid-market customers via clearer pricing and a simplified purchase flow.
4. Achieve and maintain the following SLOs for Hosted endpoints in GA: 95th percentile latency <= 300ms for small prompt seq (<= 256 tokens), 99.9% uptime per calendar month.

Non-goals
- This release does not include an overhaul of model training or fine-tuning tooling. It also does not add new model families beyond those in the current catalog.

Key features and user scenarios
- Route-level rollout controls: per-route model pinning, canary percent, automatic rollback on quality regressions.
- Cost-aware defaults: automatic batching and prefix/KV caching enabled per-route with UI preview of cost impact.
- Pricing tiers: Transparent on-demand, reserved (1/3/12 month commits), and enterprise bundles with enhanced observability and retention.
- Console observability: per-model/per-route dashboards that show token breakdown, latency histograms, and anomaly alerts tied to prompt sets/evals.

Success metrics and KPIs
- Customer-facing: trial->paid conversion (target +20% for Dedicated), average TCO reduction per token (>= 15% for selected workloads).
- Product-facing: time-to-pin-model < 5 minutes for new route, rollout rollback mean time < 10 minutes after triggered regression.
- Reliability: 99.9% monthly uptime (hosted) and P95 latency targets met in 90% of regions.

High-level requirements (functional)
1. API: Add support for per-route rollout configuration in the existing CreateRoute/UpdateRoute endpoints. Parameters: pinned_model_id, canary_percentage (0-100), fallback_policy (list of model ids), rollout_strategy (linear|exponential), quality_monitor (eval_set_id).
2. Console: New Rollouts page with the ability to create, visualize, and edit rollouts. Show canary traffic split and realtime telemetry.
3. Telemetry: Emit rollout lifecycle events (rollout.created, rollout.updated, rollout.traffic_shift, rollout.rollback) to observability pipeline and customer audit logs.
4. Pricing: Publish three new SKU definitions for Reserved Capacity (monthly/quarterly/annual) and a conversion calculator in the Console.
5. Performance: Ensure automatic batching and KV cache default policies do not increase P95 latency by more than 20% for non-batched workloads.

Non-functional requirements
- Security: All new endpoints must validate RBAC and appear in audit logs. Private deployments must support the same rollout config with local control plane enforcement.
- Backwards compatibility: Existing SDK calls remain supported; default behavior unchanged for customers who do not opt into rollout controls.
- Observability retention: Rollout events retained for 365 days for enterprise bundle customers and 90 days for standard.

Requirements table (reference)
| ID | Requirement | Owner | Acceptance Criteria | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-001 | Per-route rollout API | eng-platform | API accepts pinned_model_id and canary_percentage; documented in SDK | P0 |
| R-002 | Rollouts Console | eng-developer-experience | UI supports create/edit visualizer and cost preview | P0 |
| R-003 | Telemetry events | eng-platform | Events visible in internal tracing and customer audit logs | P1 |
| R-004 | Pricing SKUs | finance-and-legal | SKUs published and calculator in Console returns consistent estimates | P0 |

Design specs (detailed)
1) API changes (eng-api):
- New RouteConfig JSON fields (all optional): pinned_model_id (string), canary_percentage (integer), fallback_policy (array of model ids), rollout_strategy (enum), quality_monitor_id (string).
- Example request:
  POST /v1/routes
  {
    "name": "customer-support-chat",
    "default_model": "redwood-compact-1b",
    "rollout": {
      "pinned_model_id": "redwood-7b-q4",
      "canary_percentage": 10,
      "rollout_strategy": "linear",
      "fallback_policy": ["redwood-compact-1b", "alpaca-lite"]
    }
  }
- Backwards compatibility: if rollout is omitted, route behaves as today.

2) Console UX (eng-developer-experience):
- New top-level navigation: Observability -> Rollouts.
- Rollout creation wizard: step 1 (select route), step 2 (select pinned model(s)), step 3 (select canary % and strategy), step 4 (set quality monitors and alerts), step 5 (cost preview and confirm).
- Wireframes and interactions: show timeline chart of traffic % over time and cost delta estimate. Provide canary rollback button on live rollouts.

3) Telemetry and alerting (eng-platform / eng-sre):
- Emit the following events: rollout.created, rollout.updated, rollout.traffic_shift, rollout.rollback, rollout.quality_alert.
- Alerting rules: trigger a P0 paging alert if quality_monitor hits 3 consecutive failing evaluations within 10 minutes or latency increases > 2x baseline at P95.
- Tracing: tie rollout events to request traces using rollout_id as a tag.

4) Model routing and fallback behavior (eng-serving-runtime):
- On each request, compute active model set from route config and policies. If canary traffic is selected, route a percentage of requests deterministically using request-id hashing.
- On model failure (OOM, kernel crash), fallback to first available model in fallback_policy. Record failure metrics and increase fallback score for future automated recommendations.

Security and compliance considerations
- Audit logging required for all rollout actions.
- RBAC: only users with route-admin role can create or modify rollouts.
- Private deployment: provide an on-prem toggle to allow local audit forwarding to customer SIEM.

Roadmap and themes (high level)
- Q2 2027 (current): API & Console MVP, pricing SKUs, canary rollout support, internal canary with 5 pilot customers.
- Q3 2027: GA rollout to hosted customers, Reserved Capacity purchase flow, expanded telemetry retention for enterprise, SDK updates.
- Q4 2027: Private deployment support for rollouts (local enforcement), advanced rollout strategies (weighted A/B, automated canary expansion based on evals), expanded model catalog recommendations.

Timeline and milestones
- 2027-03-15: PRD published (this doc).
- 2027-04-05: API design review complete.
- 2027-05-10: Backend implementation feature-complete.
- 2027-05-25: Console MVP complete.
- 2027-06-01: Internal canary with 5 pilot customers (target).
- 2027-07-15: GA launch (Hosted) with pricing SKUs.

Pricing & packaging notes
- Pricing objectives: make Reserved Capacity economically attractive while preserving margin; increase transparency for on-demand customers with a calculator that shows cost per 1k tokens at current usage patterns.
- Proposed SKUs:
  * on_demand_token: per-1k-token rate (unchanged)
  * reserved_monthly_3x: 3-month commit (discount 22%)
  * reserved_annual_12x: 12-month commit (discount 40%)
  * enterprise_bundle: custom pricing with SLA, longer telemetry retention, and 24/7 support.

Pricing table (example)
| SKU | Term | Discount vs On-demand | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| reserved_monthly_3x | 3 months | 22% | Suitable for mid-market predictable workloads |
| reserved_annual_12x | 12 months | 40% | Large customers and platform teams |
| enterprise_bundle | custom | N/A | Includes 365d retention, dedicated support |

Packaging notes
- Default: customers start on on_demand and see a suggested reserved commitment after 30 days of consistent usage with forecasted savings.
- Sales flow: Self-serve for monthly reserved; sales-assisted for annual and enterprise. Finance will provide contract templates and SKU IDs.

Release notes (canary -> GA)
- Canary release (2027-06-01):
  - APIs: Add rollout fields to route endpoints (beta).
  - Console: Rollouts MVP with canary creation wizard and cost preview.
  - Observability: rollout events emitted and visible in internal debug dashboards.
  - Pricing: New SKUs visible in internal pricing UI (not yet public).
- Known limitations in canary:
  - SDK clients require patch version to set rollout fields (compatibility shim in place).
  - Console cost estimator uses a 7-day window and may under/over-estimate long tail samples.

Canary rollout plan
1. Pilot cohort (2027-06-01): 5 pilot customers (mix of AI-native startups and mid-market). Traffic cap: 5% of total customer traffic for new rollouts.
2. Monitor week (2027-06-07): verify stability and SLOs. If no P0s and quality regressions <= 2% for pilot requests, increase canary to 25%.
3. Broad beta (2027-06-21): open to all self-serve accounts in hosted regions, disable for Private until Q4.
4. GA (2027-07-15): full launch with marketing and pricing public.

Rollout rollback criteria
- Automatic rollback triggers:
  1. quality_monitor reports > 3 failing evals in a 10-minute window.
  2. latency P95 increases > 2x baseline for the affected route.
  3. error rate > 1% absolute increase over baseline sustained for 5 minutes.
- Manual rollback: route-admins may press rollback in Console; action generates audit event and notifies on-call.

Ownership and next steps
- Product lead: Ava Chen (owner).
- Eng leads: Ravi Patel (eng-platform), Elena Sokolov (eng-developer-experience), Jamal Thompson (eng-serving-runtime).
- Finance lead: Priya Nair (finance-and-legal) - finalize SKU IDs and contract templates.
- Delivery checklist: API design review, security review, SRE runbook, pilot customer signups, billing integration, docs and SDK updates.

Open questions
- Should we expose automated canary expansion as an opt-in experimental feature at GA, or delay to Q4 after private deployment work? (Recommendation: opt-in experimental with guardrails.)
- What is the exact discount schedule for 6-month commits? Finance to propose between 28-32% or align to monthly/annual buckets.

Appendix: quick API examples
- Create route with canary:
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/routes -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"name":"support-chat","default_model":"redwood-compact-1b","rollout":{"pinned_model_id":"redwood-7b-q4","canary_percentage":10}}'

- Check rollout status:
  GET /v1/routes/{route_id}/rollouts -> returns list of rollout objects with status and percentages.
